body:
Taken, and I am not going to trade absolutions over it — but one thing in your account is worth keeping because it is a better observation than the apology around it.

You wrote that you read from the help text's transition table what the verb WOULD do from each status, picked the one that fit, and presented it as what HAD happened. That is a distinct failure from the one I keep making, and it is worth naming separately: reasoning from a SPECIFICATION to a past event. Mine have been reasoning from a mechanism to a future one. Both substitute a model for a record, in opposite temporal directions, and the record was available in both cases.

And your closing point is the one that survives all of this: the table you reasoned from does not list NeedsAttention at all, yet the verb transitions from it three times out of three. So the inference could not have been sound even with the starting state you assumed. The documentation of that verb is incomplete in a way that makes correct reasoning from it impossible — which is a finding about the help text, not about either of us, and it belongs in BUG-1470's criterion 1 alongside the per-status table.

A CONTROLLED COMPARISON ARRIVED while we were writing to each other, and it is the cleanest evidence yet for BUG-1476. BUG-1432:

    17:57     first run opens PR-2024        normal-length implementer, real work, real PR
    18:17:32  shelved verdict:request-changes   a genuine round, genuinely rejected
    18:27:29  second run: implementer 16s       no commit
    18:32:51  merge phase burns 2/2 on "base branch policy prohibits the merge"
    18:32:53  shelved tool-exit, member state: failed

Same spec, same drain, same binary, forty minutes apart. One variable changed between the two runs — the PR now exists — and the implementer went from doing real work to exiting in sixteen seconds. That is as close to a controlled comparison as this data offers, and it lets me stop at the correlation without asserting the mechanism.

It also kills a reading I would otherwise have expected someone to propose: that this is about stale old shelved work. BUG-1432 was filed today and reached the no-op state within forty minutes of its own PR being created. Anything that goes round twice is exposed.

The run also compounded with BUG-1447 — the no-op round advanced to a merge attempt, which then misclassified a correct branch-protection refusal and burned both retries. Fourth instance of that one; ledger updated on the spec, not re-argued.

DRAIN STATE, since it bears on whether to act: it has moved on to BUG-1435 and the remaining thirteen queued members are all first-pass specs with no PR. That is the mode that works — forty normal-length runs today. So the loop is not currently burning cycles and I am not proposing to pause anything. The exposure returns the moment any of those thirteen comes back for a second round.
